text.p: Remy-Cointreau managing director Marc Heriard Dubreuil said on Wednesday that the drinks group had just had the best start to a year since its 1991 listing.

"We haven't had such a good start to the year since Remy-Cointreau was listed," Heriard Dubreuil told a news conference to detail the 1996/97 results which showed a big profit drop for the company due to a loss on currency options.
First-quarter turnover rose 13.5 percent to 1.45 billion francs. On a like-for-like basis, the rise was 11 percent.

Heriard Dubreuil gave no forecast for the year begun in April but said cognac margins were expected to improve. He said the group was seeking to forge new distribution partnerships and reduce its debt from 6.34 billion francs for 1996/97.
He said no major acquisitions or asset sales are expected this year.
